written: 2026-09-30, before eval/teacher_ceiling.py was run on any 0.5B bridge. No 0.5B run directory holds a teacher_ceiling.json; the only control any of them has is the content control of the full-width one (results/stage2c_qwen0.5b_all/compress.json). A first draft of these rules was reviewed before it was committed and before anything was measured; what is here is the text after that review and after a second one, which ran the rules against the code on constructed tables and the chain against a stand-in for the measurement, also before anything was measured.
what: The temperature control of the PsiLM-2 paper (section 'What the channel reads, and what its fit measures'), which was run on the 9B bridges only, run on the nine 0.5B bridges of its section 'The Constitution Bridge at 0.5B'. The paper says of three 0.5B comparisons that they 'have not been checked against it': the value neurons' small signal, the plain partner's advantage of 0.0040, and the split into 63% magnitude and 37% identity. This says beforehand how each will be read.
why_a_control: The bridges are trained on cross-entropy to the teacher's greedy tokens, which falls when a model is merely made surer of the tokens it mostly picks anyway. At 9B, with the backbone and the coupled system each read at its own best temperature, 0.040 of the full-width gain of 0.094 is left on red-team prompts and the narrow writes keep 0.012 or less.
the_rules_as_applied: the commit that holds this file together with eval/teacher_ceiling.py, results/constitution/arms_controls.py, eval/tempcontrol_reading.py and the chain results/constitution/tempcontrol_qwen0.5b.sh. Where this file does not state a choice, that code states it: the bootstrap is numpy's default_rng with seed 0, 2000 draws; an interval is the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of the draws; each end of an interval is rounded to six decimals, as the table stores it, before it is compared with zero or with 0.0004; an interval with zero at one of its ends includes zero; 'the record is reproduced' means within 0.0005. The chain refuses to start, to measure an arm, and to build the table or the reading, unless every one of these files is as committed, and it logs the commit. It holds what the measurement imports from this repository to the same commit (eval/bench_common.py, eval/build_constitution_data.py, psilm/__init__.py, and __init__.py, constitution.py, bridges.py, model.py, staged.py, gemma_loader.py, qwen35_loader.py and bonsai_loader.py of psilm/mlx). An arm begun under another commit is kept or resumed only if the measurement and these imports hold the same content in both. Otherwise, and when an arm has rows or a result and no record of the commit it was begun under, the chain stops before it measures anything more; such an arm is measured again only after its rows and its result are removed.

known_beforehand.as_evaluated: cross-entropy to the teacher's continuation, 100 items a split (results/stage2c_qwen0.5b_<arm>/eval_test.json, eval_helpful.json, which hold four decimals; the gains here are differences of those). Red-team split: base 0.9431; whole stream 0.5845 (gain 0.3586); whole stream with the plain partner 0.5748 (0.3683); nine value neurons 0.9249 (0.0182); nine value neurons with the plain partner 0.9209 (0.0222); top 45 value neurons 0.8828 (0.0603); nine magnitude-matched, draws 0, 1, 2: 0.9294, 0.9312, 0.9344 (0.0137, 0.0119, 0.0087); nine random 0.9406 (0.0025). Helpful split: base 0.7885; whole stream 0.5912; plain 0.5803; nine value neurons 0.7714; plain 0.7700; top 45 0.7483; matched draw 0 0.7819; random 0.7880. Matched draws 1 and 2 have no evaluator run on the helpful split.
known_beforehand.paired_as_evaluated: results/constitution/paired_bootstrap_qwen0.5b.json and the paper, written here in GAINS (base cross-entropy minus coupled cross-entropy), as the contrasts below are; the paper gives the same numbers as differences of cross-entropy, with the opposite sign. At nine coordinates the plain partner's gain exceeds the value neurons' by +0.0040, 95% [+0.0009, +0.0079]; at full width by +0.0096, [-0.0125, +0.0302]; the value neurons' gain exceeds matched draw 0's by +0.0045, [+0.0017, +0.0073], and draws 1 and 2's by +0.0063 and +0.0095.
known_beforehand.at_0.5b_the_write_uses_what_it_reads: another prompt's tokens move the full-width output by 0.035 of the write's 0.222 (results/stage2c_qwen0.5b_all/compress.json), unlike 9B. Nothing says beforehand which way the temperature control will come out here.

runs.script: eval/teacher_ceiling.py --ckpt results/stage2c_qwen0.5b_<arm>/bridges.npz --data data/constitution_test_qwen0.5b.json,data/constitution_helpful_test_qwen0.5b.json --n 100, by the chain results/constitution/tempcontrol_qwen0.5b.sh, for the arms all, allplain, vn, plainpartner, vn5, magmatch, magmatch1, magmatch2, rand
runs.items: all 100 items of each split: the evaluator's own
runs.temperatures: the script's grid, 0.30 to 1.60 in steps of 0.05, on the whole continuation; each split's temperatures are chosen on the OTHER split (cross-fitted), one for the backbone and one for the coupled system. The readings are on these cross-fitted gains. Each arm's gain with both sides at their in-split best temperatures, and what the cross-fit costs each side, are reported beside them; nothing is read from them. A gain at the best temperatures is a difference of two values taken at minima over the grid; a minimum over the grid lies above its curve's own, by up to about 0.0004 at 9B (0.0003 for the backbone), and not by the same amount on the two sides, so a bridge that only changes the temperature can show a gain of that size. The same holds, between two coupled systems, for a contrast. An interval of a gain or of a contrast that excludes zero and ends within 0.0004 of it is read as it says, and the reading flags it (ends_within_the_grids_resolution_of_zero; for the matched mean's gain, in the split, matched_mean_gain_ends_within_the_grids_resolution_of_zero). The flag is a property of the numbers and is given for an arm that is not ok too.
runs.table: results/constitution/arms_controls.py --set qwen0.5b writes results/constitution/arms_controls_qwen0.5b.json: per arm and split the gain as evaluated, the gain at the best temperatures and its 95% interval (paired bootstrap over items, both splits resampled so that the choice of the temperatures is inside the interval, every arm on the same draws), and the contrasts below
runs.an_arm_is_ok_if: its teacher_ceiling.json exists and says ok, which means: the student prompt is rebuilt as stored; teacher-forced on the stored continuation, the stored token is the teacher's argmax or within 0.25 logits of it at 97% of positions or more; the base arm on the stock and on the staged forward agree to 0.002 in mean cross-entropy; the evaluator's cross-entropies are reproduced to 0.001 where an evaluator run exists (every arm and split except the helpful split of matched draws 1 and 2). The excerpt, the system block and the backbone are checked against the builder's record before anything loads, and the script stops without writing a result if they differ. The greedy re-decode of the first two items of each split does not depend on the arm; it is recorded and reported, and is not part of ok.
runs.an_arm_that_is_not_ok: is reported as that and nothing is read from it. Every arm is measured whether or not an earlier one is ok. A contrast or a named reading that uses an arm that is not ok is reported with its numbers and read as 'not read, not ok: <arm>'. C3 and the split need the value neurons and all three matched draws to be ok, and so do the two counts beside C3 (how many per-draw intervals exclude zero with the sign; how many draws lie below the value neurons).

contrasts.C1_plain_partner_at_nine: gain(plainpartner) minus gain(vn). As evaluated +0.0040 on the red-team split, interval excluding zero.
contrasts.C2_plain_partner_at_full_width: gain(allplain) minus gain(all). As evaluated +0.0096, interval INCLUDING zero: the paper's claim is that the two are 'genuinely indistinguishable'. It has readings of its own, below.
contrasts.C3_identity_at_nine: gain(vn) minus the mean gain of the three magnitude-matched draws. As evaluated +0.0068. Its interval resamples items with the three draws held fixed, so it is a statement about these three draws and does not include the draw-to-draw spread (standard deviation 0.0025 as evaluated, comparable to the term itself). Reported beside it, with the same bootstrap and the same wording: gain(vn) minus each draw's gain; how many of the three intervals exclude zero with the as-evaluated sign; the standard deviation of the three draws' gains.
contrasts.split: the red-team split (constitution_test) is the one the paper's paired numbers are on and is the one read; the helpful split is reported beside it
contrasts.as_evaluated_again: each contrast is also computed at temperature 1 from the same rows on the same draws, so that the table shows its own as-evaluated number beside the controlled one. It should be within 0.0005 of the record's (results/constitution/paired_bootstrap_qwen0.5b.json, mean_ce: 0.004032, 0.009631, 0.006761, 0.015720, 0.042135 for C1 to C5, and 0.004529, 0.006299, 0.009454 for gain(vn) minus the gain of draws 0, 1 and 2), and the as-evaluated share of the split within 0.01 of 0.6289. Whether each is, and whether all nine are, is the first thing the reading states.

reading.an_arm: per arm and split, by the 95% interval of its gain at the best temperatures. Wholly above zero: 'keeps a gain'. Including zero: 'not distinguishable from zero at best temperature'. Wholly below zero: 'below the backbone at best temperature' (the coupled system is further from the teacher's greedy tokens than the backbone, each read at its own best temperature).
reading.a_contrast: for C1, C3, C4 and C5 on the red-team split, whose as-evaluated difference the record has as established. By the 95% interval of the paired difference at the best temperatures: 'survives' if it excludes zero on the side of the as-evaluated difference (the table's own, at temperature 1); 'does not survive' if it includes zero; 'reverses' if it excludes zero on the other side. It is the interval's side that is read, not the point's. The same words are used beside C3 for gain(vn) minus each draw's gain, and on the helpful split (reported, not read) for a contrast, C2 included, whose as-evaluated interval in the table excludes zero, against the table's own as-evaluated sign on that split. A contrast whose as-evaluated difference in the table is exactly 0.000000 has no sign; it is labelled 'no as-evaluated sign: includes zero' or 'no as-evaluated sign: excludes zero'.
reading.a_contrast_that_was_a_null: for C2 on the red-team split, and on the helpful split (reported, not read) for any contrast whose as-evaluated interval in the table includes zero. Interval at the best temperatures including zero: 'still indistinguishable' (for C2: the paper's claim holds). Excluding zero, positive: 'the first arm keeps more at the best temperatures' (for C2 the plain partner: indistinguishability fails, 'removing it costs nothing' holds). Excluding zero, negative: 'the second arm keeps more at the best temperatures' (for C2 the fine-tuned partner: 'removing it costs nothing at either width' fails at full width).
reading.the_value_neurons_small_signal: 'survives' if the nine-value-neuron arm keeps a gain on the red-team split; otherwise that arm's label under the first rule
reading.the_identity_sign: the paper says the identity term's sign is firm because all three matched draws are worse than the value neurons. It is read as 'firm at best temperature' only if C3 survives AND all three per-draw intervals exclude zero with the as-evaluated sign. If C3 survives and fewer than three do, the reading says how many. If C3 does not survive or reverses, the sign is 'not firm at best temperature'. A C3 with no as-evaluated sign counts as not surviving, here and in the split.
reading.the_63_to_37_split: the magnitude share is the mean gain of the three matched draws over the value neurons' gain, both at the best temperatures. Its 95% interval is taken on the table's own draws: the set of r for which the interval of (matched mean gain minus r times the value neurons' gain) includes zero, over r from -3 to 5 in steps of 0.001; an end that does not close in that range is reported as open. The same is computed at temperature 1 (as evaluated the paper has 62.8%, from cross-entropies rounded to four decimals; the unrounded record gives 62.9%). The share is stated as a split, 'X% magnitude, (100-X)% identity', only if all three hold: the value-neuron arm keeps a gain, the matched mean keeps a gain (its interval is above zero), and C3 survives. Otherwise the share and its interval are reported with the first label that applies: 'undefined at best temperature' (the value neurons keep no gain); 'identity term reversed at best temperature' (C3 reverses); 'identity term not distinguishable from zero at best temperature' (C3 does not survive); 'magnitude term below the backbone at best temperature' (the matched mean's interval is wholly below zero); 'magnitude term not distinguishable from zero at best temperature' (the matched mean's interval includes zero). A value-neuron gain of 0.000000 in the table gives no share (null); if none of the labels above applies to it, it is reported as 'no share: not a split'. If all three conditions hold and the share is still outside 0 to 1, it is reported as 'outside 0 to 1: not a split'. Where it is stated as a split and its interval is not contained in 0 to 1, the size of the split is reported as not determined. A share outside 0 to 1 is never stated as a split.
reading.share_kept: per arm, the gain at the best temperatures over the gain as evaluated (the table's share_surviving, from the unrounded gains), reported; no threshold is set on it. It is not the field sharpening_share of teacher_ceiling.json, which is the backbone's own gain from temperature over the raw gain.
reading.a_best_temperature_at_the_edge_of_the_gr: reported beside the number. Under the cross-fit the flag means that the OTHER split's best temperature lay at an end of the grid. If the read split's own lies at the same end, a flag on the backbone means the gain is if anything overstated, and a flag on the coupled system that it is understated; otherwise, or with both flagged, no direction is stated. The reading states the direction per arm and split (at_the_grids_edge), where there is one, and states none for an arm that is not ok. The backbone's term cancels in a contrast, so only the coupled systems' flags bear on C1 to C5.
reading.no_reading_is_changed_after_the_runs: a reading that turns out to be badly posed is reported as posed, with what was wrong with it said beside it

divergence_from_the_teacher: KL(teacher || arm) against KL(teacher || backbone) at temperature 1, per arm and split, as at 9B, where every arm's was larger than the backbone's. The cross-fitted fraction of that distance removed at the best temperatures for that distance is reported beside it (positive: the arm is nearer the teacher than the backbone): each side is at the temperature that minimises its own KL to the teacher on the other split, which need not be the one that is best for its cross-entropy. Whether an arm's is below the backbone's is stated per arm with no threshold.
not_tested: the content controls on any 0.5B bridge but the full-width one; the validation split; behaviour (no generation is made here beyond the re-decode of two items a split); the dual stack; any temperature outside the grid; the spread between matched draws beyond the three that exist
what_follows: the result is reported in results/constitution/tempcontrol_qwen0.5b_reading.json, and the sentences of the two cards of ryoji-info/PsiLM-2 that say the control was not run at 0.5B are written from it
